Jamie — thanks again for taking the call today. Short recap and the information I said I'd follow up with so we can lock a sketch quote: 

Summary of requirements from our discussion:
- Deployment: Private VPC (self-managed infra with Redwood private control plane)
- Expected monthly inference volume (approx): 250–500M tokens (this is the inference-side estimate; please let me know if you track input/output separately)
- Environments: Prod + Staging + Dev (you mentioned 3, please confirm)
- SLA/support: interested in 24x7 response for incidents (likely Enterprise/Premier tier)
- Compliance: audit logs + customer-managed KMS

Target unit economics (what you mentioned on the call): target $/1M tokens <= $300 (goal inclusive of Palo Alto-style support/managed ops). You said the internal procurement budget target is in the mid-$30k/month range but may flex for a committed discount. 

What I will do next:
- Send an initial license + committed-capacity outline (attached draft proposal + SOW) that shows two licensing options (per-environment subscription vs pooled enterprise commit) and corresponding unit pricing ladders.
- Ask Marissa/Neha to produce a committed quote example for 250M and 500M tokens to show how committed discounts change $/1M.

Quick asks for you: please confirm the final environment count and whether staging needs the same capacity as prod (full replica) or can be smaller. Also confirm whether Procurement wants contract language around data residency/retention beyond the SOC2 controls we discussed.

Attachments: Proposal-Acme-Health-draft.pdf (outline + example math), SOW-Acme-Health-draft.docx (ops & support scope)

Best,
Connor

Thanks, Connor — good summary. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Volumes: our initial run rate target is closer to 300M inference tokens/month (this is after we stabilize the first two production features). Peak could reach 500M in 6–9 months depending on adoption.
- Environments: confirm 3 environments — prod (full capacity), staging (50% capacity), dev (non-prod; small).
- Budget: Procurement is initially targeting $25k–$40k/month all-in. If we can get committed pricing that brings $/1M below $300, procurement will make room for a 12-month commit.
- Licensing model preference: we prefer a pooled enterprise license (single contract for the org) rather than separate per-env SKUs — simpler for procurement. However we need visibility into per-env costs for chargeback.
- Support: we want Premier (24x7 + named TAM) if it fits the budget. Please confirm what Premier includes vs Standard.

We can review a committed example (250M and 500M) and an evergreen flex option. Also include any one-time onboarding/enablement fees.

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Carter <jamie.carter@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-18T17:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — private VPC pricing options + unit economics

Jamie — great, thanks for the clarifications. Below is a short, concrete sketch (will follow with a formal quote). Numbers are illustrative to show the math:

Option 1 — Pooled enterprise commit (preferred by procurement)
- Commitment: 12-month term, committed throughput examples: 250M tokens/mo or 500M tokens/mo
- Unit price (example): $/1M tokens = $325 for 250M commit; $/1M tokens = $275 for 500M commit
- Platform fee (license): $6,000/month for production env + $3,000/month for staging replica (if staging mirrors prod capacity), dev included at $500/month
- Example math (500M commit): token charge = 500 * $275 = $137,500/month + platform licenses (prod $6k + staging $3k + dev $0.5k = $9.5k) => ~$147k/month (note: draft numbers — committed pricing usually blends infra + license so final SOW will show net lower effective cost per 1M)

Option 2 — Per-environment subscriptions + pay-as-you-go usage
- Flat env licenses: prod $8k/mo, staging $4k/mo, dev $750/mo
- Usage price (no commit): $/1M tokens = $450 (burstable, on-demand)

Support tiers
- Standard: 24x5 incident handling, quarterly business reviews, shared Slack channel, 8–24 hour SLAs depending severity
- Premier: 24x7 coverage, named TAM, quarterly on-site/remote enablement sessions, 1-hour P1 response and monthly architecture reviews (this is the one you flagged). Premier typically adds a % uplift on the license or is a fixed monthly add-on — we'll show both approaches.

Next steps I need from you to finalize a formal quote:
1) Approve 3 env counts and confirm whether staging must be full replica (you said 50% in the note above).
2) Confirm whether you want committed pricing examples for 250M and 500M (yes/no).
3) Procurement team point of contact for redlines.

I'll loop in Marissa to produce the committed vs on-demand spreadsheet and Neha to confirm support/enablement deliverables and pricing.

Connor
